content.content:
### The toolbar

From left to right:

- **Transport**: Go to Start (Home), Previous Edit Point (↑), Play / Pause
  (Space), Next Edit Point (↓), Go to End (End), and **Loop**. Loop is dimmed
  while off.
- **Timecode**: the playhead's time, then `/` and the duration of what the
  timeline shows. Click the time to type one: it takes `HH:MM:SS:FF`,
  `HH:MM:SS.mmm`, `HH:MM:SS`, `MM:SS`, seconds with a decimal (`83.5`) or a
  bare number of seconds. Press Return to jump there, snapped to a frame.
  Text that is not a time beeps and the field goes back to the playhead's
  time.
- **Preview zoom**: a popup with Fit, 50%, 100% and 200%.
- **Safe**: shows the title-safe and action-safe guides (90 % and 80 %
  rectangles) on the preview. Remembered between launches.
- **Export…** (⌘E): see [Export](export.md).

Timecode shows frames by default. The Document tab's **Timecode** popup
(Frames or Milliseconds) changes every readout, the ruler included.

### The timeline bar

From left to right:

- **The selection block**, naming what is selected (see
  [Selecting clips](#selecting-clips)).
- **Eight clip buttons**: Split (⌘T), Trim Start to Playhead (W), Trim End
  to Playhead (E), Ripple Delete (⌘⌫), Add Marker (M), Duplicate (⌘D), Add
  Text (T) and Add Shape. Each button's tooltip names its key. **Add Shape**
  opens a menu of shapes and has no menu-bar item, so this button is the way
  to add one. What the edits do is on [Editing](editing.md); text and shapes
  are on [Canvas and layers](canvas-and-layers.md).
- **Snap**, the snapping checkbox (see [Snapping](#snapping)).
- **The level meter** (see [The level meter](#the-level-meter)).
- **The zoom cluster**: −, the zoom slider, + and Fit (⇔) (see
  [Zooming the timeline](#zooming-the-timeline)).
- **S / M / L**, the track size (see [Row heights](#row-heights)).

## The ruler and the playhead

The ruler's ticks adjust to the zoom, from single frames up to minutes.
Labels drop the hours when the timeline is under an hour long. The playhead
is the coral line with a triangle head on the ruler.

- **Click the ruler** to move the playhead there, and **drag** along it to
  scrub. Playback stops while you scrub, and you hear the sound under the
  playhead instead (see [Hearing a scrub](audio.md#hearing-a-scrub)). The
  scrub snaps like any other drag
  (see [Snapping](#snapping)).
- The timeline scrolls itself to keep the playhead in view: when the playhead
  leaves the visible part, during playback or after a jump, the view moves
  so the playhead sits about a third of the way in.
- A click in a lane doesn't move the playhead. It starts a marquee selection
  (see [Selecting clips](#selecting-clips)).

## Playback

| Key | What it does |
|---|---|
| Space | Play / pause |
| J | Play backwards; press again for 2×, then 4× |
| K | Pause |
| L | Play forwards; press again for 2×, then 4× |
| ← / → | Back / forward one frame (pauses) |
| ⇧← / ⇧→ | Back / forward ten frames |
| ↑ / ↓ | Previous / next edit point |
| Home / End | Go to the start / end |

**Edit points** are the start and end of the timeline and the start and end
of every clip. ↑ with nothing earlier goes to the start.

J pressed while playing forwards, or L while playing backwards, switches
direction at 1×.

Space plays and pauses wherever the focus is, except while you type in a
text field or when a focused button uses the key itself. Typing ends with
Return, Tab or a click outside the field (on the timeline, say), and Space
plays straight after it. On the preview
canvas a quick Space press still plays or pauses (when you let go), while
holding Space and dragging pans the canvas instead. Holding Space down
doesn't toggle playback over and over. Letter keys never
fire while you are typing in a field, and no editor key works while a sheet
is open.

Playback stops at the end of the timeline. An empty timeline has nothing to
play: Play beeps.

### Loop

Turn on **Loop** in the toolbar to loop playback. With an in/out range set it
loops the range; otherwise it loops the whole timeline. Pressing play at or
past the end of the loop starts again from the loop's start. Loop is set per
window and isn't saved.

### What you'll notice after an edit

- A change that only alters how something looks (a property, a colour, text)
  redraws the frame in place without interrupting playback.
- A change to the timeline's structure (a move, a trim, a new clip) rebuilds
  the player in the background. It keeps your place and keeps playing at the
  same rate. While you drag, the rebuild waits until you pause briefly.
- If a rebuild fails, an error is shown and the previous version keeps
  playing.

*Agents:* `set_playhead {t}` moves the playhead and seeks the preview.
`get_project` reports the playhead, selection and in/out range along with the
project. `render_frame` writes the frame at a time as a PNG.

## Zooming the timeline

| Way | How |
|---|---|
| Pinch | On a trackpad, about the pointer |
| ⌥-scroll or ⌘-scroll | Zoom about the pointer |
| Zoom slider | The slider in the timeline bar |
| − / + buttons | Either side of the slider, in steps about the middle of the view |
| Fit Timeline | ⇧Z, the ⇔ button, or **View ▸ Fit Timeline**. Fits the whole timeline in the view and scrolls to the start. |

A window opens at a fixed zoom of about 42 pt per second, not fitted to the
project, so press ⇧Z to see all of a long project. The zoom runs from about a
third of a point per second (hours on screen) to 4,000 pt per second (single
frames wide).

A plain scroll moves the view. **View ▸ Zoom In** (⌘+ or ⌘=), **Zoom Out**
(⌘-) and **Zoom to Fit** (⌘0) zoom the *preview*, not the timeline. They step
through the same stops as the toolbar's zoom popup (see
[Canvas and layers](canvas-and-layers.md)).

## Selecting clips

| To | Do this |
|---|---|
| Select a clip | Click it |
| Add or remove a clip | ⇧-click it |
| Select with a marquee | Drag from any empty space: a gap in a lane, the strip under the ruler, or the space below the last lane. A plain drag replaces the selection; ⇧-drag adds to it. Clips on locked tracks are skipped. |
| Clear the selection | Click empty space |
| Select everything | **Edit ▸ Select All** (⌘A): every clip, on locked tracks too |
| Select everything from the playhead on | **Edit ▸ Select After Playhead** (⌥⌘A): every clip whose start is at or after the playhead, on every track including locked ones. A clip under the playhead isn't included. |
| Select a track's clips | ⌥-click its header, or **Edit ▸ Select All on Track** |

The **selection block** at the left of the timeline bar names what is
selected: one clip's name over its track and kind (`Track 2 · video`), or a
count such as `3 clips` over the track (or `2 tracks`) and the kind (or
`mixed`). With nothing selected it reads "No selection". Selecting clips on
the timeline switches the inspector to its Clip tab.

**Edit ▸ Select All on Track** selects every clip on the current track: the
first selected clip's track, or the front track when nothing is selected. It
beeps when that track is empty. ⌥-clicking a header uses the track you
clicked.

Selection is view state: it is never an undo step and isn't saved.

*Agents:* `set_selection {clips}` (an empty list selects nothing).

## Snapping

Snapping is on by default. While on, a drag (move, trim, roll, marker or
scrub) jumps to a nearby **clip edge**, **marker**, **the playhead**,
**an in/out point**, or **the start or end of the timeline** when it comes within about 8 pt, and a thin guide line
shows what it caught. A drag that doesn't snap still lands on a whole frame.

| To | Do this |
|---|---|
| Turn snapping on or off | N, the **Snap** checkbox in the timeline bar, or **View ▸ Snapping** (checked when on) |
| Skip snapping for one drag | Hold ⌘ while you drag |

The setting is remembered between launches.

## Markers
## Keys without a menu item

These keys work in the editor window when you are not typing in a field.
They also work in the Preview Window.

A field takes the keys only when you click in it, or choose a command that
opens one for typing (Clip ▸ Rename…, View ▸ Assistant). Return, keypad Enter, Tab
or a click anywhere outside the field applies what you typed and gives the
keys back to the editor, so Space plays straight away. In a multi-line
field (the Text tab's Content, the Assistant's message), Return applies and
⇧Return starts a new line. With Full Keyboard Access on, Tab moves to the
next control instead.

### Playback and moving the playhead

| Key | What it does |
|---|---|
| Space | Play / pause, wherever the focus is in the window. In a text field, Space types a space. A button focused with Full Keyboard Access keeps Space to press itself |
| L | Plays forward. Press it again for 2× and then 4× |
| J | Plays in reverse. Press it again for 2× and then 4× in reverse |
| K | Pauses |
| ← / → | Moves back or forward one frame. With ⇧, ten frames |
| ↑ / ↓ | Moves to the previous or next edit point |
| Home / End | Moves to the start or end of the project |

When the preview canvas has focus, the arrow keys move the selected clips
instead ([below](#preview-canvas-gestures)).

### Editing
## Timeline gestures

| Gesture | Where | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| Click | Clip | Selects it |
| ⇧-click | Clip | Adds it to the selection, or removes it |
| Click | Empty lane | Deselects everything |
| Drag | Empty lane, or above or below the tracks | Marquee: selects every clip the band touches. Clips on locked tracks are skipped |
| ⇧-drag | Empty lane | Marquee that adds to the selection |
| Double-click | Empty part of a lane | Closes that gap |
| Drag | Clip | Moves the selected clips, in time and to other tracks. Dragging past the top or bottom track puts them on a new track |
| ⌥-drag | Clip | Duplicates the clips and moves the copies |
| ⌥⇧-drag | Clip | Slip: moves the source under the clip while the clip stays in place |
| Drag | Clip edge | Trims that edge |
| ⌥-drag | Clip's end edge | Rate stretch: changes the speed so the clip fills the new length. Works only on a clip that plays a media file. On the start edge, ⌥ trims as usual |
| ⌥⇧-drag | Clip edge | Roll: moves the cut between this clip and the clip touching it. Does nothing where there is no touching clip |
| Drag | Fade handle on a clip | Sets that clip's audio fade-in or fade-out |
| Drag | Volume line on a clip | Changes the level in force there, in dB (see [Audio](audio.md#the-volume-line)) |
| ⌥-click or ⌥-drag | Volume line on a clip | Adds a volume point there as an action, then sets its level |
| Click | Action band | Selects the clip and that action. The Clip tab then edits the action's end values; ⎋ deselects the action |
| Drag | Action band | Moves the action in time |
| Drag | Edge of an action band | Changes the action's length |
| Double-click | Clip | Renames it in place |
| Double-click | Nest clip | Goes inside the nest. To rename a nest clip, use ⇧⌘R |
| Click or drag | Ruler | Moves the playhead (scrubbing), playing the sound under it |
| Drag | Marker | Moves it |
| Double-click | Marker | Renames it |
| Drag | Track header | Moves the track up or down the stack |
| Double-click | Track header | Renames the track |
| ⌥-click | Track header | Selects every clip on that track |
| Click | Header buttons (eye, speaker, lock, headphones, sliders) | Hide Video, Mute Audio, Lock Track, Solo, and the mix panel |
| Click | Breadcrumb in the corner, while a nest is open | Comes back out by one level |
| Hold ⌘ while dragging | Any drag that snaps | Turns snapping off for that drag, even when you press ⌘ partway through |
| Pinch, or ⌥ / ⌘ with the scroll wheel | Anywhere on the timeline | Zooms around the pointer |
| Scroll | Anywhere on the timeline | Scrolls |

While snapping is on (N), moving, trimming and rolling clips, dragging a
marker and scrubbing the ruler snap to clip edges, markers, the start and
end of the timeline, the playhead and the in/out points, within about 8
points of the pointer. A slip doesn't snap.

Clips on a locked track can't be dragged, trimmed, slipped or rolled. Every
drag is one undo step. See [Editing](editing.md) and [The timeline](timeline.md).

*Agents:* `move_clip`, `trim_start`, `trim_end`, `rate_stretch`, `slip`,
`roll`, `close_gap`, `set_action`, `set_audio` (fades), `move_track`,
`set_playhead`.

## Buttons with no menu item
## What is remembered

| Setting | Remembered between launches |
|---|---|
| Timeline height, inspector width, inspector hidden | Yes |
| Snapping, track size, Safe Areas, Preview Quality | Yes, for every project |
| Preview Window position | Yes |
| Timeline zoom, Loop, playhead, selection, in/out range | No |

## Limits

- Markers live on the main timeline only. Inside a nest the ruler shows
  none, drags don't snap to them, and you can't add one, step to one or jump
  to one; the Document tab can still rename, chapter and delete them.
- Clips on a locked track can be clicked and selected, but not dragged or
  trimmed, and a marquee skips them.
- A marker's colour can only be changed by an agent.
- The timeline zoom has no menu item or keyboard shortcut except ⇧Z (fit).

See [Menus and shortcuts](menus-and-shortcuts.md) for every key in one place.

---
title: "Jump around the timeline"
description: "Move the playhead straight to the next cut, either end of the timeline, or a time you type."
---

import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';

These are the quick ways to put the playhead where you want it: hop from cut to cut, go to either end of the timeline, or type a time. To drag it along the ruler, see [The ruler and playhead](/timeline/ruler-and-playhead/). To step frame by frame, see [Play, pause and shuttle](/timeline/playback/). To hop between flags, see [Markers](/timeline/markers/).

<AtAGlance
  keys={['↑', '↓', 'Home', 'End']}
  where={['The transport buttons in the toolbar', 'The timecode field in the toolbar']}
  tools="set_playhead"
/>

## Jump between edit points

Press <kbd>↑</kbd> for the previous edit point and <kbd>↓</kbd> for the next. The **Previous Edit Point** and **Next Edit Point** buttons either side of Play in the toolbar do the same.

An edit point is the start or end of any clip, on any track, and the two ends of the timeline.

- <kbd>↑</kbd> with nothing earlier goes to the start of the timeline.
- <kbd>↓</kbd> on the last edit point stays where it is.
- Playback keeps going. The playhead jumps and plays on from there.
- With a [nest](/editing/nests/) open, these step through the nest's clips.

## Go to the start or end

Press <kbd>Home</kbd> for the start of the timeline and <kbd>End</kbd> for the end, or use the **Go to Start** and **Go to End** buttons at the two ends of the transport. Both pause playback first.

The keypad's Home and End work too, and so does the <kbd>fn</kbd> key with <kbd>←</kbd> or <kbd>→</kbd> on a keyboard without them. With a nest open, they go to the start and end of the nest.

## Type a time to jump

The toolbar shows the playhead's time in a field. You can type into it.

<Steps>

1. Click the time.

2. Type where you want to go.

3. Press <kbd>Return</kbd>, or click anywhere outside the field.

</Steps>

Playback pauses, the playhead moves to the nearest frame, and the keys go back to the editor, so <kbd>Space</kbd> plays straight away.

The field takes any of these, whichever way the project displays time. Fields don't need leading zeros.

| You type | Example | It means |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Hours, minutes, seconds and frames | `00:01:23:12` | 1 minute 23 seconds and 12 frames |
| Hours, minutes and seconds with milliseconds | `00:01:23.500` | 1 minute 23.5 seconds |
| Hours, minutes and seconds | `1:23:04` | 1 hour 23 minutes 4 seconds |
| Minutes and seconds | `1:23` | 1 minute 23 seconds |
| Seconds with a decimal | `83.5` | 83.5 seconds |
| A bare number of seconds | `83` | 83 seconds |

Text that isn't a time beeps, and the field goes back to the playhead's time. Only whole numbers count as frames, so `00:00:01:12.5` isn't a time.

A leading minus sign is accepted, but the playhead can't go before the start, so a negative time lands on the first frame.

The field shows frames by default. The [Document tab's **Timecode** row](/projects/background-and-timecode/) switches it to milliseconds, along with every other time readout. The field stops following the playhead while you type in it.

## Read the duration

After the time, the toolbar shows a slash and the length of what the timeline shows, such as `/ 00:00:05:07`. It's written the same way as the time, in frames or milliseconds.

With a [nest](/editing/nests/) open, both numbers are the nest's: the time counts from the nest's own start, and the duration is the nest's length.

## With an agent

`set_playhead` moves the playhead to a time and seeks the preview. It doesn't pause playback. Agent tools that work at a time, such as `split`, `freeze_frame` and `add_marker`, use the playhead when they're given no time. See [Tools: playhead, range and selection](/mcp/tools-view-state/).

## Good to know

- Moving the playhead is never an edit. It makes no undo step, and it isn't saved with the project.
- When a jump lands outside the visible part of the timeline, the view scrolls to bring the playhead back.
- With the preview canvas in focus and a clip selected, the arrow keys [nudge the clip](/canvas/move-scale-rotate/) instead of moving the playhead.
- With the text of the [Transcript tab](/captions/transcript-keys/) in focus, the arrow keys move through its words.
- None of these keys work while you're typing in a field or while a sheet is open. They do work in the [Preview Window](/timeline/preview-window/).

## Related

- [The ruler and playhead](/timeline/ruler-and-playhead/)
- [Play, pause and shuttle](/timeline/playback/)
- [Markers](/timeline/markers/)
- [The in/out range](/timeline/in-out-range/)

---
title: "Loop playback"
description: "Repeat the in/out range or the whole timeline while you watch and adjust."
---

import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';

Loop keeps playback going round, so you can watch a passage over and over while you adjust it.

<AtAGlance where="The Loop button in the toolbar" />

## Turn Loop on

Click **Loop**, the repeat button at the end of the transport in the toolbar. The button is dimmed while Loop is off and full strength while it's on. Click it again to turn Loop off.

Loop has no menu item and no key. It's off when a window opens, it's set for each window on its own, and it isn't saved with the project.

## What it repeats

| What's set | What Loop repeats |
| --- | --- |
| An [in/out range](/timeline/in-out-range/) | The range |
| No range, or a range of no length | The whole timeline |

With a [nest](/editing/nests/) open, the whole timeline means the whole nest. Entering or leaving a nest clears the range.

The loop follows as things change. Set a new in or out point, clear the range or change the timeline's length while Loop is on, and the next pass uses the new span.

## How playback goes round

When playback reaches the end of the loop, it jumps back to the loop's start and carries on, at 2× and 4× as well.

- Press play at or past the end of the loop and it starts again from the loop's start.
- Press play before the start of the loop and it plays from where the playhead is. It only jumps back once it reaches the loop's end.
- Loop only works forwards. Playing backwards with <kbd>J</kbd> doesn't go round, and carries on past the start of the loop.

## Good to know

- The **Preview** button in the [**Motion presets**](/motion/motion-presets/) section, and **Clip ▸ Motion ▸ Preview**, set the in/out range to the clip and turn Loop on. Both stay until you clear them.
- Selecting words in the Transcript tab sets the range, so Loop plays those words. See [Follow along and jump](/captions/follow-the-transcript/).

## Related

- [The in/out range](/timeline/in-out-range/)
- [Play, pause and shuttle](/timeline/playback/)

Zoom the timeline out to see a whole project at once, or in to place a cut on a single frame. Everything on this page changes the timeline only. To zoom the picture, see [Zoom and pan the preview](/canvas/zoom-and-pan/).

<AtAGlance
  menu="View ▸ Fit Timeline"
  keys="⇧Z"
  where={['The zoom controls at the right of the timeline bar', 'Pinch, or ⌥ or ⌘ and scroll, over the timeline']}
/>

## Zoom about the pointer

Put the pointer on the part of the timeline you care about, then either:

- pinch on a trackpad, or
- hold <kbd>⌥</kbd> or <kbd>⌘</kbd> and scroll.

The time under the pointer stays where it is while everything else spreads out or closes in around it, which makes this the best way to get close to one cut.

## Use the zoom slider

Drag the **Timeline Zoom** slider in the timeline bar. It zooms about the middle of the view, and it covers the whole zoom range on a log scale, so the same travel always changes the zoom by the same ratio.

## Step with the − and + buttons

The **Zoom Out** and **Zoom In** buttons sit either side of the slider. Each click moves the zoom by 5 % of the slider's travel, which is about 1.6 times, and keeps the middle of the view in place. Twenty clicks cross the whole range.

## Fit the whole project

Press <kbd>⇧Z</kbd>, click **Fit Timeline** (the ⇔ button after the + button), or choose **View ▸ Fit Timeline**. The whole project fits across the timeline pane and the view scrolls to the start.

The menu item shows no key, because <kbd>⇧Z</kbd> is one of the keys the editor handles itself. This is the only timeline zoom with a menu item or a key.

A project under 1 second long fits as if it were 1 second. With a [nest](/editing/nests/) open, Fit Timeline fits the nest.

:::note
**View ▸ Zoom In**, **Zoom Out** and **Zoom to Fit** zoom the preview, not the timeline.
:::

## How far it zooms

A window opens at 42 points per second, not fitted to the project, so press <kbd>⇧Z</kbd> to see all of a long project.

The zoom runs from 0.35 points per second, with hours on screen, to 4,000 points per second, with a single frame wider than a clip thumbnail needs. Past either limit, nothing changes.

The zoom isn't saved. Every window opens at 42 points per second again, and an agent has no tool to set it.

## Scroll the timeline

Scroll, or swipe with two fingers, over the timeline. The track headers stay at the left and the ruler stays at the top while the lanes move.

The timeline keeps some empty room past the last clip, so you can reach the end and drag a clip beyond it.

The view also moves by itself to keep the playhead in sight. See [The ruler and playhead](/timeline/ruler-and-playhead/).

## Related

- [The ruler and playhead](/timeline/ruler-and-playhead/)
- [Jump around the timeline](/timeline/move-the-playhead/)
- [Track height](/timeline/track-height/)
- [Zoom and pan the preview](/canvas/zoom-and-pan/)

---
title: "Select clips"
description: "Pick the clips you want to work on by clicking, dragging a marquee, or choosing a whole track or everything after the playhead."
---

import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';

The selection tells Frame Job which clips you mean. The inspector, the handles on the canvas and the commands in the menus all work on it. Selecting a clip changes nothing in the project.

<AtAGlance
  menu={['Edit ▸ Select All', 'Edit ▸ Select After Playhead', 'Edit ▸ Select All on Track']}
  keys={['⌘A', '⌥⌘A']}
  where={['Click, ⇧-click or drag on the timeline', '⌥-click a track header']}
  tools="set_selection"
/>

## Click a clip

Click a clip to select it alone. It gets an outline, and the timeline bar names it.

Clicking a clip that's already part of a larger selection keeps the whole selection, so you can drag the clips together. To get down to one clip, click empty space first, then click the clip.

You can click a clip on a [locked track](/timeline/hide-and-lock-tracks/) to select it and read it in the inspector, but you can't drag or trim it.

A double-click doesn't select. It [renames the clip](/timeline/names-and-labels/), or goes inside a [nest](/editing/nests/).

## Add or remove with ⇧-click

<kbd>⇧</kbd>-click a clip to add it to the selection. <kbd>⇧</kbd>-click a selected clip to take it out.

## Drag a marquee

Drag from any empty part of the timeline: a gap in a lane, the strip under the ruler, or the space below the last lane. A band follows the pointer and selects every clip it touches, even a clip it only clips the corner of.

- A plain drag replaces the selection.
- <kbd>⇧</kbd>-drag adds to the selection. Clips already selected stay selected.
- Clips on locked tracks are skipped.

## Clear the selection

Click an empty part of a lane, or the space above or below the lanes.

:::caution
A double-click in an empty part of a lane [closes that gap](/editing/close-gaps/). That's an edit, not a deselect. Press <kbd>⌘Z</kbd> if you did it by accident.
:::

## Select all the clips

**Edit ▸ Select All** (<kbd>⌘A</kbd>) selects every clip in the timeline you're editing, on locked tracks too. With a nest open, it selects the clips inside the nest.

While you're typing in a field, <kbd>⌘A</kbd> selects the field's text instead. With the [Transcript tab](/captions/transcript-keys/)'s text in focus, it selects the words.

## Select everything after the playhead

**Edit ▸ Select After Playhead** (<kbd>⌥⌘A</kbd>) selects every clip whose start is at or after the playhead, on every track, including locked ones. A clip the playhead is partway through isn't included.

Use it to push the rest of a project along: select everything after the playhead, then [drag it to make room](/editing/close-gaps/).

## Select all the clips on a track

<kbd>⌥</kbd>-click a track's header to select every clip on that track, locked or not. On an empty track, this leaves nothing selected.

**Edit ▸ Select All on Track** does the same for the current track, which is the track of a selected clip, or the front track when nothing is selected. It's dimmed when the timeline has no clips, and it beeps when the current track is empty.

## See what's selected

The left end of the timeline bar names the selection.

| Selected | The bar shows |
| --- | --- |
| One clip | A chip in the clip's kind colour, the clip's name, and its track and kind under it, such as `Track 2 · video` |
| Several clips | A count such as `3 clips`, over the track (or `2 tracks`) and the kind (or `mixed`) |
| Nothing | `No selection` |

This block is a fixed width, so a long name is cut short and the tools beside it never move.

## How a selection behaves

A selection isn't an edit. It's never an undo step, it doesn't mark the project as changed, and it isn't saved, so a project always opens with nothing selected.

- Selecting on the timeline switches the inspector to its **Clip** tab, unless the Transcript tab is showing. The Edit menu's commands leave the inspector on the tab it's on.
- The timeline and the canvas share one selection. See [Select on the canvas](/canvas/select-on-canvas/).
- A clip that's deleted drops out of the selection.
- Going into a nest or coming back out changes the selection, because the clips on show are different.

## With an agent

`set_selection` sets the selection, and with no clips it clears it. An agent doesn't need it to edit, because its tools name their own clips. It matters for what depends on the selection, such as the canvas handles and the inspector. With a nest open, it selects inside the nest. See [Tools: playhead, range and selection](/mcp/tools-view-state/).

## Related

- [Select on the canvas](/canvas/select-on-canvas/)
- [Select an action](/motion/select-an-action/)
- [Move clips](/editing/move-clips/)
- [Hide and lock tracks](/timeline/hide-and-lock-tracks/)

---
title: "Snapping"
description: "Make timeline drags catch clip edges, markers, the playhead and the in and out points, and turn it off when you don't want it."
---

import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';

Snapping makes a drag catch the useful points on the timeline, so a clip lines up with the next cut instead of landing a frame away from it. This page is about the timeline. For dragging on the picture, see [Canvas snapping](/canvas/canvas-snapping/).

<AtAGlance
  menu="View ▸ Snapping"
  keys="N"
  where="The Snap checkbox in the timeline bar"
/>

## Turn snapping on or off

Press <kbd>N</kbd>, click the **Snap** checkbox in the timeline bar, or choose **View ▸ Snapping**, which has a tick when snapping is on. The menu item shows no key, because <kbd>N</kbd> is one of the keys the editor handles itself.

Snapping is on by default, and your choice is remembered between launches. One setting serves both the timeline and the canvas. There's no agent tool for it.

## What a drag snaps to

These drags snap:

- moving clips
- trimming a clip's edge
- a [rate stretch](/speed/rate-stretch/)
- a [roll](/editing/slip-and-roll/)
- dragging a [marker](/timeline/markers/)
- scrubbing along the [ruler](/timeline/ruler-and-playhead/)

They catch these points:

- the start and the end of the timeline
- the edges of other clips, but never of the clips you're dragging
- markers
- the playhead
- the in and out points

A point catches when it's within 8 points on screen. That's the same distance at every zoom, so when you're zoomed out it covers more time. If two points are equally close, the earlier one wins.

When you move clips, it's the start of the earliest clip you're dragging that snaps, and the whole group moves with it. The end of a moved clip doesn't catch anything. To line up an end, trim it, or move the clip with the start against the point you want.

Inside a [nest](/editing/nests/), there are no markers to catch, and the other points are the nest's.

## Turn snapping off for one drag

Hold <kbd>⌘</kbd> during the drag. It works from the moment you press or at any time during the drag, and it takes effect at once. Let go of <kbd>⌘</kbd> and the drag snaps again.

This works on the canvas too, and it changes nothing that's remembered.

## See what a drag caught

When a drag snaps, a thin vertical line runs across the timeline at the point it caught. Scrubbing the ruler snaps too, but it draws no line. The playhead is already there to show you.

## Drags land on whole frames

A drag that doesn't snap still lands on a whole frame. That's true with snapping off, while you're holding <kbd>⌘</kbd>, and when nothing is close enough to catch.

## What never snaps

- A [slip](/editing/slip-and-roll/) never snaps.
- A row from the [Media tab](/projects/media-tab/) dropped on a lane lands on the nearest frame at the pointer, and doesn't snap to edges.
- Dragging an [action band](/motion/action-lane/) lands on whole frames, and doesn't snap.
- Dragging a [fade handle](/audio/fades/) or the [volume line](/audio/volume-line/) doesn't snap.

## Good to know

A window reads the setting when it opens. If two projects are open, changing it in one leaves the other as it is until you open that project again.

## Related

- [Canvas snapping](/canvas/canvas-snapping/)
- [Move clips](/editing/move-clips/)
- [Trim clips](/editing/trimming/)
- [Slip and roll](/editing/slip-and-roll/)
- [Markers](/timeline/markers/)

---
title: "Jump around the timeline"
description: "Move the playhead straight to the next cut, either end of the timeline, or a time you type."
---

import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';

These are the quick ways to put the playhead where you want it: hop from cut to cut, go to either end of the timeline, or type a time. To drag it along the ruler, see [The ruler and playhead](/timeline/ruler-and-playhead/). To step frame by frame, see [Play, pause and shuttle](/timeline/playback/). To hop between flags, see [Markers](/timeline/markers/).

<AtAGlance
  keys={['↑', '↓', 'Home', 'End']}
  where={['The transport buttons in the toolbar', 'The timecode field in the toolbar']}
  tools="set_playhead"
/>

## Jump between edit points

Press <kbd>↑</kbd> for the previous edit point and <kbd>↓</kbd> for the next. The **Previous Edit Point** and **Next Edit Point** buttons either side of Play in the toolbar do the same.

An edit point is the start or end of any clip, on any track, and the two ends of the timeline.

- <kbd>↑</kbd> with nothing earlier goes to the start of the timeline.
- <kbd>↓</kbd> on the last edit point stays where it is.
- Playback keeps going. The playhead jumps and plays on from there.
- With a [nest](/editing/nests/) open, these step through the nest's clips.

## Go to the start or end

Press <kbd>Home</kbd> for the start of the timeline and <kbd>End</kbd> for the end, or use the **Go to Start** and **Go to End** buttons at the two ends of the transport. Both pause playback first.

The keypad's Home and End work too, and so does the <kbd>fn</kbd> key with <kbd>←</kbd> or <kbd>→</kbd> on a keyboard without them. With a nest open, they go to the start and end of the nest.

## Type a time to jump

The toolbar shows the playhead's time in a field. You can type into it.

<Steps>

1. Click the time.

2. Type where you want to go.

3. Press <kbd>Return</kbd>, or click anywhere outside the field.

</Steps>

Playback pauses, the playhead moves to the nearest frame, and the keys go back to the editor, so <kbd>Space</kbd> plays straight away.

The field takes any of these, whichever way the project displays time. Fields don't need leading zeros.

| You type | Example | It means |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Hours, minutes, seconds and frames | `00:01:23:12` | 1 minute 23 seconds and 12 frames |
| Hours, minutes and seconds with milliseconds | `00:01:23.500` | 1 minute 23.5 seconds |
| Hours, minutes and seconds | `1:23:04` | 1 hour 23 minutes 4 seconds |
| Minutes and seconds | `1:23` | 1 minute 23 seconds |
| Seconds with a decimal | `83.5` | 83.5 seconds |
| A bare number of seconds | `83` | 83 seconds |

Text that isn't a time beeps, and the field goes back to the playhead's time. Only whole numbers count as frames, so `00:00:01:12.5` isn't a time.

A leading minus sign is accepted, but the playhead can't go before the start, so a negative time lands on the first frame.

The field shows frames by default. The [Document tab's **Timecode** row](/projects/background-and-timecode/) switches it to milliseconds, along with every other time readout. The field stops following the playhead while you type in it.

## Read the duration

After the time, the toolbar shows a slash and the length of what the timeline shows, such as `/ 00:00:05:07`. It's written the same way as the time, in frames or milliseconds.

With a [nest](/editing/nests/) open, both numbers are the nest's: the time counts from the nest's own start, and the duration is the nest's length.

## With an agent

`set_playhead` moves the playhead to a time and seeks the preview. It doesn't pause playback. Agent tools that work at a time, such as `split`, `freeze_frame` and `add_marker`, use the playhead when they're given no time. See [Tools: playhead, range and selection](/mcp/tools-view-state/).

## Good to know

- Moving the playhead is never an edit. It makes no undo step, and it isn't saved with the project.
- When a jump lands outside the visible part of the timeline, the view scrolls to bring the playhead back.
- With the preview canvas in focus and a clip selected, the arrow keys [nudge the clip](/canvas/move-scale-rotate/) instead of moving the playhead.
- With the text of the [Transcript tab](/captions/transcript-keys/) in focus, the arrow keys move through its words.
- None of these keys work while you're typing in a field or while a sheet is open. They do work in the [Preview Window](/timeline/preview-window/).

## Related

- [The ruler and playhead](/timeline/ruler-and-playhead/)
- [Play, pause and shuttle](/timeline/playback/)
- [Markers](/timeline/markers/)
- [The in/out range](/timeline/in-out-range/)

---
title: "Loop playback"
description: "Repeat the in/out range or the whole timeline while you watch and adjust."
---

import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';

Loop keeps playback going round, so you can watch a passage over and over while you adjust it.

<AtAGlance where="The Loop button in the toolbar" />

## Turn Loop on

Click **Loop**, the repeat button at the end of the transport in the toolbar. The button is dimmed while Loop is off and full strength while it's on. Click it again to turn Loop off.

Loop has no menu item and no key. It's off when a window opens, it's set for each window on its own, and it isn't saved with the project.

## What it repeats

| What's set | What Loop repeats |
| --- | --- |
| An [in/out range](/timeline/in-out-range/) | The range |
| No range, or a range of no length | The whole timeline |

With a [nest](/editing/nests/) open, the whole timeline means the whole nest. Entering or leaving a nest clears the range.

The loop follows as things change. Set a new in or out point, clear the range or change the timeline's length while Loop is on, and the next pass uses the new span.

## How playback goes round

When playback reaches the end of the loop, it jumps back to the loop's start and carries on, at 2× and 4× as well.

- Press play at or past the end of the loop and it starts again from the loop's start.
- Press play before the start of the loop and it plays from where the playhead is. It only jumps back once it reaches the loop's end.
- Loop only works forwards. Playing backwards with <kbd>J</kbd> doesn't go round, and carries on past the start of the loop.

## Good to know

- The **Preview** button in the [**Motion presets**](/motion/motion-presets/) section, and **Clip ▸ Motion ▸ Preview**, set the in/out range to the clip and turn Loop on. Both stay until you clear them.
- Selecting words in the Transcript tab sets the range, so Loop plays those words. See [Follow along and jump](/captions/follow-the-transcript/).

## Related

- [The in/out range](/timeline/in-out-range/)
- [Play, pause and shuttle](/timeline/playback/)

---
title: "Zoom and scroll the timeline"
description: "Zoom the timeline out to see a whole project or in to single frames, and scroll along it."
---

import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';

Zoom the timeline out to see a whole project at once, or in to place a cut on a single frame. Everything on this page changes the timeline only. To zoom the picture, see [Zoom and pan the preview](/canvas/zoom-and-pan/).

<AtAGlance
  menu="View ▸ Fit Timeline"
  keys="⇧Z"
  where={['The zoom controls at the right of the timeline bar', 'Pinch, or ⌥ or ⌘ and scroll, over the timeline']}
/>

## Zoom about the pointer

Put the pointer on the part of the timeline you care about, then either:

- pinch on a trackpad, or
- hold <kbd>⌥</kbd> or <kbd>⌘</kbd> and scroll.

The time under the pointer stays where it is while everything else spreads out or closes in around it, which makes this the best way to get close to one cut.

## Use the zoom slider

Drag the **Timeline Zoom** slider in the timeline bar. It zooms about the middle of the view, and it covers the whole zoom range on a log scale, so the same travel always changes the zoom by the same ratio.

## Step with the − and + buttons

The **Zoom Out** and **Zoom In** buttons sit either side of the slider. Each click moves the zoom by 5 % of the slider's travel, which is about 1.6 times, and keeps the middle of the view in place. Twenty clicks cross the whole range.

## Fit the whole project

Press <kbd>⇧Z</kbd>, click **Fit Timeline** (the ⇔ button after the + button), or choose **View ▸ Fit Timeline**. The whole project fits across the timeline pane and the view scrolls to the start.

The menu item shows no key, because <kbd>⇧Z</kbd> is one of the keys the editor handles itself. This is the only timeline zoom with a menu item or a key.

A project under 1 second long fits as if it were 1 second. With a [nest](/editing/nests/) open, Fit Timeline fits the nest.

:::note
**View ▸ Zoom In**, **Zoom Out** and **Zoom to Fit** zoom the preview, not the timeline.
:::

## How far it zooms

A window opens at 42 points per second, not fitted to the project, so press <kbd>⇧Z</kbd> to see all of a long project.

The zoom runs from 0.35 points per second, with hours on screen, to 4,000 points per second, with a single frame wider than a clip thumbnail needs. Past either limit, nothing changes.

The zoom isn't saved. Every window opens at 42 points per second again, and an agent has no tool to set it.

## Scroll the timeline

Scroll, or swipe with two fingers, over the timeline. The track headers stay at the left and the ruler stays at the top while the lanes move.

The timeline keeps some empty room past the last clip, so you can reach the end and drag a clip beyond it.

The view also moves by itself to keep the playhead in sight. See [The ruler and playhead](/timeline/ruler-and-playhead/).

## Related

- [The ruler and playhead](/timeline/ruler-and-playhead/)
- [Jump around the timeline](/timeline/move-the-playhead/)
- [Track height](/timeline/track-height/)
- [Zoom and pan the preview](/canvas/zoom-and-pan/)

---
title: "Select clips"
description: "Pick the clips you want to work on by clicking, dragging a marquee, or choosing a whole track or everything after the playhead."
---

import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';

The selection tells Frame Job which clips you mean. The inspector, the handles on the canvas and the commands in the menus all work on it. Selecting a clip changes nothing in the project.

<AtAGlance
  menu={['Edit ▸ Select All', 'Edit ▸ Select After Playhead', 'Edit ▸ Select All on Track']}
  keys={['⌘A', '⌥⌘A']}
  where={['Click, ⇧-click or drag on the timeline', '⌥-click a track header']}
  tools="set_selection"
/>

## Click a clip

Click a clip to select it alone. It gets an outline, and the timeline bar names it.

Clicking a clip that's already part of a larger selection keeps the whole selection, so you can drag the clips together. To get down to one clip, click empty space first, then click the clip.

You can click a clip on a [locked track](/timeline/hide-and-lock-tracks/) to select it and read it in the inspector, but you can't drag or trim it.

A double-click doesn't select. It [renames the clip](/timeline/names-and-labels/), or goes inside a [nest](/editing/nests/).

## Add or remove with ⇧-click

<kbd>⇧</kbd>-click a clip to add it to the selection. <kbd>⇧</kbd>-click a selected clip to take it out.

## Drag a marquee

Drag from any empty part of the timeline: a gap in a lane, the strip under the ruler, or the space below the last lane. A band follows the pointer and selects every clip it touches, even a clip it only clips the corner of.

- A plain drag replaces the selection.
- <kbd>⇧</kbd>-drag adds to the selection. Clips already selected stay selected.
- Clips on locked tracks are skipped.

## Clear the selection

Click an empty part of a lane, or the space above or below the lanes.

:::caution
A double-click in an empty part of a lane [closes that gap](/editing/close-gaps/). That's an edit, not a deselect. Press <kbd>⌘Z</kbd> if you did it by accident.
:::

## Select all the clips

**Edit ▸ Select All** (<kbd>⌘A</kbd>) selects every clip in the timeline you're editing, on locked tracks too. With a nest open, it selects the clips inside the nest.

While you're typing in a field, <kbd>⌘A</kbd> selects the field's text instead. With the [Transcript tab](/captions/transcript-keys/)'s text in focus, it selects the words.

## Select everything after the playhead

**Edit ▸ Select After Playhead** (<kbd>⌥⌘A</kbd>) selects every clip whose start is at or after the playhead, on every track, including locked ones. A clip the playhead is partway through isn't included.

Use it to push the rest of a project along: select everything after the playhead, then [drag it to make room](/editing/close-gaps/).

## Select all the clips on a track

<kbd>⌥</kbd>-click a track's header to select every clip on that track, locked or not. On an empty track, this leaves nothing selected.

**Edit ▸ Select All on Track** does the same for the current track, which is the track of a selected clip, or the front track when nothing is selected. It's dimmed when the timeline has no clips, and it beeps when the current track is empty.

## See what's selected

The left end of the timeline bar names the selection.

| Selected | The bar shows |
| --- | --- |
| One clip | A chip in the clip's kind colour, the clip's name, and its track and kind under it, such as `Track 2 · video` |
| Several clips | A count such as `3 clips`, over the track (or `2 tracks`) and the kind (or `mixed`) |
| Nothing | `No selection` |

This block is a fixed width, so a long name is cut short and the tools beside it never move.

## How a selection behaves

A selection isn't an edit. It's never an undo step, it doesn't mark the project as changed, and it isn't saved, so a project always opens with nothing selected.

- Selecting on the timeline switches the inspector to its **Clip** tab, unless the Transcript tab is showing. The Edit menu's commands leave the inspector on the tab it's on.
- The timeline and the canvas share one selection. See [Select on the canvas](/canvas/select-on-canvas/).
- A clip that's deleted drops out of the selection.
- Going into a nest or coming back out changes the selection, because the clips on show are different.

## With an agent

`set_selection` sets the selection, and with no clips it clears it. An agent doesn't need it to edit, because its tools name their own clips. It matters for what depends on the selection, such as the canvas handles and the inspector. With a nest open, it selects inside the nest. See [Tools: playhead, range and selection](/mcp/tools-view-state/).

## Related

- [Select on the canvas](/canvas/select-on-canvas/)
- [Select an action](/motion/select-an-action/)
- [Move clips](/editing/move-clips/)
- [Hide and lock tracks](/timeline/hide-and-lock-tracks/)

---
title: "Snapping"
description: "Make timeline drags catch clip edges, markers, the playhead and the in and out points, and turn it off when you don't want it."
---

import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';

Snapping makes a drag catch the useful points on the timeline, so a clip lines up with the next cut instead of landing a frame away from it. This page is about the timeline. For dragging on the picture, see [Canvas snapping](/canvas/canvas-snapping/).

<AtAGlance
  menu="View ▸ Snapping"
  keys="N"
  where="The Snap checkbox in the timeline bar"
/>

## Turn snapping on or off

Press <kbd>N</kbd>, click the **Snap** checkbox in the timeline bar, or choose **View ▸ Snapping**, which has a tick when snapping is on. The menu item shows no key, because <kbd>N</kbd> is one of the keys the editor handles itself.

Snapping is on by default, and your choice is remembered between launches. One setting serves both the timeline and the canvas. There's no agent tool for it.

## What a drag snaps to

These drags snap:

- moving clips
- trimming a clip's edge
- a [rate stretch](/speed/rate-stretch/)
- a [roll](/editing/slip-and-roll/)
- dragging a [marker](/timeline/markers/)
- scrubbing along the [ruler](/timeline/ruler-and-playhead/)

They catch these points:

- the start and the end of the timeline
- the edges of other clips, but never of the clips you're dragging
- markers
- the playhead
- the in and out points

A point catches when it's within 8 points on screen. That's the same distance at every zoom, so when you're zoomed out it covers more time. If two points are equally close, the earlier one wins.

When you move clips, it's the start of the earliest clip you're dragging that snaps, and the whole group moves with it. The end of a moved clip doesn't catch anything. To line up an end, trim it, or move the clip with the start against the point you want.

Inside a [nest](/editing/nests/), there are no markers to catch, and the other points are the nest's.

## Turn snapping off for one drag

Hold <kbd>⌘</kbd> during the drag. It works from the moment you press or at any time during the drag, and it takes effect at once. Let go of <kbd>⌘</kbd> and the drag snaps again.

This works on the canvas too, and it changes nothing that's remembered.

## See what a drag caught

When a drag snaps, a thin vertical line runs across the timeline at the point it caught. Scrubbing the ruler snaps too, but it draws no line. The playhead is already there to show you.

## Drags land on whole frames

A drag that doesn't snap still lands on a whole frame. That's true with snapping off, while you're holding <kbd>⌘</kbd>, and when nothing is close enough to catch.

## What never snaps

- A [slip](/editing/slip-and-roll/) never snaps.
- A row from the [Media tab](/projects/media-tab/) dropped on a lane lands on the nearest frame at the pointer, and doesn't snap to edges.
- Dragging an [action band](/motion/action-lane/) lands on whole frames, and doesn't snap.
- Dragging a [fade handle](/audio/fades/) or the [volume line](/audio/volume-line/) doesn't snap.

## Good to know

A window reads the setting when it opens. If two projects are open, changing it in one leaves the other as it is until you open that project again.

## Related

- [Canvas snapping](/canvas/canvas-snapping/)
- [Move clips](/editing/move-clips/)
- [Trim clips](/editing/trimming/)
- [Slip and roll](/editing/slip-and-roll/)
- [Markers](/timeline/markers/)
